solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Moral member of royal family, mostly one quietly guided (10)

indicators.note: 'mostly' means not quite all of it, so the royal title loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A well-behaved royal being quietly steered through public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moral' is an adjective here, not the noun for a story's lesson, and 'mostly' cuts only the royal, not the phrase after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone of high moral standards acts on principle.

clue.text: Servant’s time under pressure (4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, what sits under something is written after it

blocks.note: an age = a long period of time

explanation.surface: A servant's working hours spent under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay, and 'under' puts the time below the pressure in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a boy employed as a servant in a great household or at court.

clue.text: New Yorker’s got rid of cold (4)

explanation.surface: An American has finally shaken off a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Yorker's' flags an American usage: in US gangster slang to ice someone is to murder them. 'Cold' looks like the illness being shaken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a regional slang verb for killing a rival, and the everyday adjective for a chilled drink.

clue.text: Opposing company, a politician offering convincing evidence? (12)

blocks.note: con = against, as in pros and cons
a Tory = a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A rival firm and a politician produce damning evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a courtroom or scandal; 'Opposing' is just the Latin-derived 'against' that also gives the con in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: evidence that settles a doubt is said to confirm it.

clue.text: Direct contribution to debate? (5)

blocks.note: a verb: to aim, show the way
something argued, as in 'a good one'

explanation.surface: A plain, forthright remark made in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct' reads as an adjective qualifying 'contribution'; it is really a verb standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to aim a finger or a camera, and a single argument made in discussion.

clue.text: He and I rested, sadly knocked out? (9)

indicators.note: 'sadly' as in 'sadly neglected', badly, so the letters are left in poor order

blocks.note: anagram fodder: HE + I + RESTED, 9 letters; 'and' just joins

explanation.surface: Two people took a rest and, unhappily, passed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ether was an early surgical anaesthetic, so the definition means put under for an operation, not punched.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put under with ether is a specific way of being knocked out.

clue.text: Partially wrap something put back in box (4)

indicators.note: 'partially' means only part of the words, so the letters sit within them
'put back' as in returned the way it came, so the found letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Wrapping an item and returning it to its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like the packaging; it is the verb, to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise in light bouts, so the verb is a gentler form of boxing.

clue.text: Ship’s compartment in a mess, so I help out (5,5)

indicators.note: things in a mess are untidy and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor volunteers to tidy a cluttered cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' fits the ship too, where it is the crew's dining room, which hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The enclosed wheelhouse on deck from which a vessel is steered is one of its compartments.

clue.text: Argues for sports field primarily offering many, many goals (10)

indicators.note: 'primarily' means in the first place, so each of the next three words gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone campaigning for a sports ground that promises lots of goals.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the rec is the local recreation ground, a public playing field. 'Goals' are aims, not scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to advise in favour of something is to argue for it.

clue.text: Permission to land on part of golf course (5,5)

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece put 'on' another is added after it

blocks.note: to light = to land, settle, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Clearance for a plane to touch down on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land on' reads as one phrase, but the landing word is written on the end of the golf term.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from traffic signals: the go-ahead to proceed.

clue.text: Political group’s announced restrictive measure (4)

indicators.note: something announced is spoken aloud, so go by how the word sounds

explanation.surface: A party has publicly declared a curb.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. The French spelling without K is the political one.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of nations or parties acting together, as in the old Eastern bloc.

clue.text: Drew on being this overcome by awe? (12)

blocks.note: the surface reads an artist sketching; the setter means these six letters as a result
a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction (a word 'struck', knocked about), produces those letters

explanation.surface: An artist sketching while stunned by what she sees.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: WONDER, struck (knocked about), gives DREW ON. The clue says DREW ON is what you get from this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: struck with wonder, amazed.

clue.text: Football manager’s season threatened with relegation? (12)

explanation.surface: A manager's team is having a season that may end in the drop.
explanation.walkthrough: In English leagues the clubs at the foot of the table are relegated to the division below.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Walter Winterbottom was England's first national team manager, 1946 to 1962.

clue.text: Greens said to be excited, given new position (10)

indicators.note: excited particles are agitated and moving about, so the letters move

explanation.surface: The Green Party is reportedly thrilled about a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' looks like the political party or vegetables; it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: moved to a different post or duty.

clue.text: Familiar chap denounced arrests (10)

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold someone, so the second piece holds the first

explanation.surface: A well-known man was denounced and taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar chap' reads as one character, a regular; 'Familiar' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when followed by 'with' or 'to': used to, familiar with.

clue.text: To go round enclosure order permit (9)

blocks.note: enc. = enclosure, as at the foot of a letter
OM = Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A notice demanding a permit to walk round a fenced area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' suggests a paddock, and 'order' a command; both are abbreviations. The Order of Merit is an exclusive British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to surround or encircle.

clue.text: Fun in the morning time entertains service staff (9)

indicators.note: a host entertains guests in the house, so the outside pieces hold the others

explanation.surface: An early fun session laid on to amuse the waiters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service staff' reads as one phrase, meaning waiters, but it splits into two words; 'entertains' fits the fun surface while doing the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: enjoyment, entertainment.

clue.text: Herd of animals runs into bird (5)

indicators.note: something that runs into a thing ends up inside it

explanation.surface: A stampeding herd crashes into a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the herd's movement; it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a herd or flock being driven along together.

clue.text: Divert leader of saboteurs ahead of illegal pursuit? (5)

indicators.note: the leader goes at the front, so take the first letter
one piece placed ahead of another comes first

blocks.note: fox hunting with hounds is illegal in Britain

explanation.surface: Hunt saboteurs try to lead the hounds away from an illegal hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunting foxes with dogs was banned in England and Wales in 2004; hunt saboteurs are activists who disrupt hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway term: to move a train onto a side track, so to divert.

clue.text: Rude nudes cavorting, having too little to do? (9)

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping and prancing about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Naked people frolicking because they are bored.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the picture from the definition, which is phrased as the reason for the frolicking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: not put to work enough.

clue.text: During period I had to restrict journalist’s go-between role (12)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the outer pieces go round the journalist

explanation.surface: A role as middleman meant a period of keeping a reporter in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' means consumed, a sense easy to miss. The whole string from 'During' to 'had' goes round the journalist, and the 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an intermediate is one who acts between two parties, a go-between.

clue.text: Privy to knowledge finally being combined (2,3)

indicators.note: 'finally' means at the end, so the word gives its last letter

explanation.surface: Being let in on a secret at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privy to' is the idiom for sharing a secret, which the surface keeps; 'finally' works only on 'knowledge'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: several features rolled into a single thing, as in an all-in-one.

clue.text: Female wrath — it is destructive (4)

explanation.surface: A warning that a woman's anger does damage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description, not a synonym: the clue invites you to name something that destroys.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: flames destroy what they burn.

clue.text: Bird in difficulty (4)

explanation.surface: A bird in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the two meanings; it reads as a bird caught in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shorebird of the sandpiper family, and a tangle that is hard to undo.

clue.text: Celeb, fellow spinning round with energy (4)

indicators.note: something spun round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A celebrity and a man twirling energetically on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply adds the energy after the turned-round fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for celebrity; a big name is a famous person.

clue.text: Transfer of power achieved finally — a slow process? (10)

indicators.note: 'finally' means at the end, so the word gives its last letter

blocks.note: change in species works over ages

explanation.surface: Handing power down to regions takes a long, slow time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word means passing powers from Westminster to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, which happened slowly, so the surface reads true.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain definition: power handed from central to regional government.

clue.text: Old bird given repeated encouragement to act? (4)

explanation.surface: An elderly person being nagged again and again to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bird' sounds like slang for an old woman; it is the long-extinct bird of Mauritius.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a flightless bird extinct since the 1600s.

clue.text: Most variable in quality but having the most marks? (10)

blocks.note: most covered in lines or smears

explanation.surface: An erratic student who nonetheless scores highest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' suggests exam scores; here they are lines on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: form that runs hot and cold, and a surface smeared with lines.
